title: Telemetry-driven metering heuristics for truncated / lazy-stream uploads
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Intermittent customer reports and internal audits show overcharges for sessions where clients upload truncated payloads or perform 'lazy' streaming (open connection, send small fragments, then abandon). Current pipeline gives provisional token debits on receipt of fragments that sometimes never finalize, and rate-limiter logic can double-deduct when reconnects/resumes happen. This ticket implements telemetry-driven heuristics and pipeline checkpoints to reduce false positive billing while keeping quota enforcement and SLOs intact.
proposed_solution: Introduce a telemetry-derived provisional vs finalized token model: mark incoming stream fragments with provisional_token_count and attach lightweight 'stream sentinel' markers (start/commit/abort) emitted by gateway. Add a short-lived checkpointing layer in the metering pipeline that defers final ledger debits until one of: explicit commit sentinel, TTL expiry with confirmed EOF, or deterministic consolidation on resume that reconciles provisional credits. Implement idempotency keys and resume_offset alignment to avoid double-deduction on reconnects. Update rate-limiter to consult provisional windows and avoid immediate hard debits for fragments below a low-size threshold unless client is over quota by confirmed usage. Expose new metrics (provisional_tokens, finalized_tokens, sentinel_mismatch_rate) and a reconciliation job that backfills or refunds provisional credits when malformed sessions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: New metrics ingested into observability: provisional_tokens, finalized_tokens, sentinel_mismatch_rate
End-to-end e2e simulation shows <=0.1% false-positive billing for truncated/lazy-stream scenario across 10k simulated sessions
Rate-limiter does not double-debit for reconnects that match resume_offset in >= 99.9% validated cases
Reconciliation job successfully identifies and refunds provisional credits for a staged 5% production canary within rollback SLA
Unit and integration tests added for: sentinel parsing, idempotency key handling, resume_offset logic, and TTL expiry path
tasks: Add sentinel marker extraction in gateway (start/commit/abort) and include sentinel headers in metering events
Implement provisional_token_count and finalized_token_count fields through the metering pipeline
Create checkpoint-storage for live streams (in-memory soft-state with durable anchors) and TTL semantics
Modify rate-limiter to read provisional windows and defer hard debits for small fragments
Add reconciliation job with dashboard and playbook for refunds
Add comprehensive unit + integration tests and a synthetic e2e harness for truncated/abandoned streams
Canary rollout plan: 1% -> 5% -> 20% traffic with staged metrics and automatic rollback condition

notes: Design trade-offs: delaying final ledger debits reduces false positives but increases reconciliation complexity and temporary exposure of provisional credits in dashboards
We must keep deterministic accounting for Dedicated customers; provisioning will be an opt-in flag per tenant initially
Edge case: interleaved multi-tenant multiplexed streams require canonicalization of sentinel markers — delegated to ENG-314159 (dependency)
Rollback criteria for canary: sentinel_mismatch_rate > 0.5% or refunds > 0.2% of billed volume over 15m window
